subject: POC kickoff recap -- scope, metrics, next steps (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff recap -- scope, metrics, next steps (Acme Corp)

Hi Alex / Samira --

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed POC scope so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you described
- High variance in generative latency during peak traffic (spikes to ~1s+ p95)
- Unit cost is unpredictable across models and traffic patterns
- Difficult to measure quality regressions across changes to prompts/models

Primary goals for the pilot
1) Reduce p95 latency for production queries to <= 300ms for the main chat route
2) Establish repeatable evals/prompt set to detect regressions (target: >=90% pass rate on golden set)
3) Measure unit cost and give configuration recommendations to hit < $0.60 / 1k tokens for expected traffic profile

Proposed POC scope (3 weeks) -- high level
- Week 0 (this week): access + baseline profiling -- provision test API key and run 1k representative requests to capture latency/cost baseline
- Week 1: integration + prompt tuning -- deploy chat and summarization routes, run prompt tuning and KV/prefix caching tests
- Week 2: evals + quality gates -- run golden set + blind evals, collect metrics and iterate; present final recommendations and next-step options (Dedicated or Hosted Sizing)

Metrics we’ll track
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per route, cold vs warm
- Cost: tokens consumed / 1k tokens, total monthly estimate for expected QPS
- Quality: pass rate on golden prompt set, A/B blind eval delta vs current baseline

Owners
- Customer lead: Alex Johnson (Acme) -- provide sample prompts, representative request logs, and test dataset
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole -- commercial lead, Milestone coordination
- Redwood SE: Aditya Rao -- integration and tuning lead
- Redwood CS/Eng: Dylan Brooks -- monitoring, tracing, and rollout plan

Access & setup checklist (what we need from Acme today)
1) A test account or API key / temporary service account for the test tenant (or org-level sample dataset in S3)
2) A sample set of ~1k representative prompts/requests (sanitized)
3) Contact for infra (for VPC peering / IP allowlist if you want to lock down access)

Attachments: POC_SOW.pdf (high-level scope + commercial terms), redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx (technical checklist)

Next steps / proposed kickoff meeting
- Please confirm you can share the test API key and sample prompts by Tue 3/23
- Proposed kickoff: Wed 3/24 10:00 AM PST -- I’ll send a calendar invite once confirmed

Thanks and excited to get started --
Marissa

--

Thanks for the clear recap -- this is exactly what we discussed and the timeline looks good. A few quick clarifications: 
- We can provide a sanitized sample of ~1k requests by Tue 3/23; Samira will own that deliverable.

I’ll confirm kickoff time once Samira confirms the data handoff.

Great -- thanks Alex. Confirming a couple of follow-ups and adding more detail on evals and telemetry so Samira / infra can action.

Telemetry items (to collect on your side)
- Per-request timestamps (client send, server receive, server send, client receive) to compute cold vs warm latency
- Request/response token counts
- Route/tag field so we can split chat vs search vs summarization
- Error codes and full stack traces for any 5xx responses during the run

Eval / prompt set plan
- Golden set: 250 curated prompts with expected outputs (used for deterministic pass/fail checks)
- Blind eval: ~1,000 randomized requests scored by your SMEs (or outsourced annotators) to estimate real-world quality lift
- Automated regression harness: Redwood runs the golden set on each candidate model/config during the POC and reports pass rate deltas

Success criteria (POC exit)
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms on main chat route under the expected test QPS profile
- Quality: >=90% pass rate on golden set or clear regression reduction vs baseline
- Cost: recommendations scoped and an expected unit cost estimate for monthly projection

On the API key: yes -- Redwood can issue a scoped, time-limited API key for the POC. Aditya, can you please provision a scoped key and share the onboarding steps?

I’ll send the kickoff invite for Wed 3/24 10:00 AM PST once Samira confirms the data delivery window. Attaching the SOW and the checklist again.

Attachments: POC_SOW.pdf, redwood-poc-checklist.xlsx

Thanks --
Marissa
